stories.Headline: NACDC 2026 Concludes at UBC, Advancing Global AI & Technology Research
stories.Summary:
The North American Conference on Computational Intelligence, Data Science and Cloud Computing concluded on August 12, 2026, after three days at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver. The event was hosted by the Institute of Engineering and Management in Kolkata, India, along with partner organizations. The conference brought together over 12,000 participants from more than 35 countries, including the United States, Canada, Australia, Malaysia, Egypt, and South Africa, to share research and discuss developments in artificial intelligence, data science, and cloud computing.

The three-day program featured keynote lectures from industry and academic leaders, paper presentations organized across four technical tracks, and workshops on topics like local AI models and robotics. Papers were selected through a rigorous peer-review process with an acceptance rate of approximately 26 percent. The event concluded with a valedictory session and Best Paper Awards. Conference proceedings will be published by Nova Science Publishers, and organizers emphasized the conference's role in fostering international collaboration and encouraging new researchers in these advancing fields.

stories.Headline: Government of Kerala Partners with SAS to Strengthen Social Welfare Schemes Delivery using Artificial Intelligence
stories.Summary:
The Government of Kerala has partnered with SAS, a global data and artificial intelligence company, to improve how social welfare programs are delivered across the state. Kerala State IT Mission selected SAS as a strategic analytics partner to strengthen governance and service delivery through advanced data analytics capabilities. The collaboration aims to streamline beneficiary management for all social protection schemes by detecting duplicate citizen records, enhancing real-time decision-making, improving compliance monitoring, and strengthening the efficiency of welfare scheme delivery.

Through this initiative, Kerala intends to consolidate data across departments to boost transparency and accountability in social welfare programs. The partnership aligns with Kerala's broader vision to use technology for inclusive growth and transparent governance. According to officials, the state aims to set a strong example for data-driven governance in India by leveraging SAS's analytics capabilities to turn complex data into meaningful insights that support better governance outcomes and citizen-focused innovation.

stories.Headline: IFSCA Grants Nexent Capital GIFT City Investment Banking License
stories.Summary:
Nexent Capital IFSC Private Limited, the GIFT City-based subsidiary of U.S.-based Nexent Capital Management, has received formal registration from the International Financial Services Centres Authority to operate as an investment banker in India's International Financial Services Centre. The registration was granted on July 31, 2026, under the Capital Market Intermediaries Regulations, 2025, allowing the firm to conduct regulated investment banking activities from GIFT City in Gujarat.

With this license, Nexent Capital is now authorized to manage initial public offerings, follow-on public offerings, SPAC listings, secondary listings, depository receipt issuances, and debt capital market transactions. The firm plans to expand its investment banking platform to support high-growth companies from the United States and Europe seeking capital-raising and listing opportunities. Nexent Capital currently has an active pipeline of companies in sectors including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data centers, quantum computing, space technology, and energy.

stories.Headline: Uttarakhand CM Dhami inaugurates Deeksharambh Session and new infrastructure at Doon University
stories.Summary:
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami inaugurated the Deeksharambh Session 2026-27 and Youth Dialogue Programme at Doon University on Thursday. He opened new infrastructure including a Biological Sciences Laboratory building costing Rs 11.20 crore and a Central Library building costing Rs 17.39 crore. The Chief Minister also launched the Doon University Community Radio Station 88.4 FM and announced that the Central Library would be named after Dr BR Ambedkar. Additionally, he declared that two electric buses would be provided for students and new positions would be created for the community radio station.

The Chief Minister announced plans to strengthen foreign language departments by creating positions for Spanish, German, French, Chinese and Japanese language programs. He emphasized the importance of youth in nation-building and highlighted government initiatives supporting young people, including providing up to Rs 50,000 assistance for interview preparation for competitive exams. He also noted that over 34,000 young people have been appointed to government services over the past five years through a transparent recruitment system.

stories.Headline: PSU Major DFCCIL Awards Letter of Acceptance to Magellanic Cloud Limited Subsidiary, Deepening Pan-India PSU Portfolio
stories.Summary:
Magellanic Cloud Limited announced that its subsidiary, Provigil Surveillance Limited, received a contract worth 3.73 crore rupees from Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited, a government-owned railway company. The contract involves supplying, installing, testing and maintaining an electronic surveillance system along a section of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor over five years. The surveillance system will provide theft prevention, remote monitoring, asset protection, perimeter security and dock management services for critical railway infrastructure.

The five-year agreement is structured as an operational expenditure model and demonstrates growing confidence from major public sector companies in Provigil's security capabilities. The contract aligns with Magellanic Cloud's broader strategy of expanding its surveillance and security solutions across railways, highways, government infrastructure and other critical sectors. The company, headquartered in Hyderabad, works with over 100 clients internationally and employs more than 1,600 professionals across its various subsidiaries specializing in digital transformation, artificial intelligence and surveillance technology.

stories.Headline: Amgen to open New Science & Innovation Center in Genome Valley, Hyderabad
stories.Summary:
Amgen announced plans to establish a new Science and Innovation Center in Hyderabad's Genome Valley region, which will become part of the company's seven-laboratory global research network. The facility is expected to open in 2027 and will integrate advanced scientific capabilities with digital innovation to accelerate medicine discovery and development. Scientists and technologists will work across discovery chemistry, drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics, and precision medicine at the center.

This expansion reflects Amgen's commitment to leveraging India's strong life sciences ecosystem and demonstrates Hyderabad's growing importance as a global research hub. The new center will work closely with Amgen's existing technology and innovation site in the same city, combining wet-laboratory science with advanced technology. Officials highlighted how this investment represents a significant step in establishing Hyderabad as a center for discovering and developing next-generation medicines for global patients.

stories.Headline: Parliamentary panel rejects govt response on cyber fraud, says it fails to plug key gaps
stories.Summary:
A Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance has rejected the government's response to tackling cyber-enabled financial fraud, stating that proposed measures are largely procedural and fail to address critical operational gaps. The Department of Financial Services highlighted various existing tools including artificial intelligence systems used by banks, the Reserve Bank of India's MuleHunter system to identify suspected mule accounts, and fraud monitoring solutions for digital transactions. However, the committee found these responses inadequate and insufficient.

The panel identified several key concerns, including inadequate accountability for banks that maintain mule accounts used in fraud schemes. Under the proposed compensation framework, banks would bear only 10 percent of losses while the RBI would bear 65 percent, creating what the committee called a severe moral hazard. Additionally, the committee flagged the failure to address the critical three-to-four-hour window, known as the Golden Hour, during which fraudulent funds could potentially be frozen and recovered. The committee recommended imposing stricter liability on banks and establishing a framework to penalize branches with repeated KYC verification lapses.

stories.Headline: Artmarket.com: Q2 2026 Upward Trend, from Progressive Transition to Artprice's "AI-FIRST" Metamorphosis
stories.Summary:
Artmarket.com announced strong second quarter 2026 performance and revealed a major strategic shift in its artificial intelligence integration. Founder Thierry Ehrmann and the controlling Groupe Serveur family plan to increase their shareholdings in the company, demonstrating confidence in its growth trajectory. The company is accelerating its transformation from a gradual AI rollout to a comprehensive "AI-First" architecture centered on its proprietary databases and two main AI systems called Intuitive Art Market and Blind Spot.

Rather than incrementally adding AI features to existing systems, Artprice is overhauling its entire operational infrastructure internally before releasing it to subscribers. The company emphasized that controlling its own data pipelines and algorithms gives it a competitive advantage in an era where much internet content contains unreliable synthetic data. The complete platform will eventually offer subscribers autonomous AI agents for market analysis, forecasting, and risk modeling through subscription fees ranging from 1,600 to 2,500 dollars annually. This transformation represents a fundamental change in how Artprice operates, evolving from a historical database into an active decision-making system.

stories.Headline: Punjab National Bank (PNB) to Deploy Magellanic Cloud's E-Surveillance Solutions Across 1,000 ATMs Nationwide
stories.Summary:
Magellanic Cloud Limited's subsidiary, IVIS International Private Limited, has secured multiple purchase orders from NCR Corporation India Private Limited to install surveillance solutions across 1,000 Punjab National Bank ATM locations nationwide. The contract is valued at approximately 18.4 crore rupees and spans five years, encompassing both capital expenditure and operational expenditure components. This deployment demonstrates IVIS's capability to execute large-scale surveillance projects across distributed banking networks.

The company, headquartered in Hyderabad, specializes in digital transformation and artificial intelligence-driven surveillance systems. According to Magellanic Cloud's Chairman and Managing Director Joseph Sudheer Reddy Thumma, the banking and financial services sector has been a strategic focus for over 15 years. The order reinforces the company's position in delivering technology-enabled security solutions for critical financial infrastructure and reflects its ability to address the growing security needs of major Indian banks. The company employs over 1,600 professionals and serves more than 100 clients across multiple countries.

stories.Headline: Will data centers increase electrical bills, water use and noise levels in North Dakota?
stories.Summary:
North Dakota State University researcher Robert Mayo created a guide examining how artificial intelligence data centers will impact the state's electricity costs, water use and noise levels. The guide serves policymakers considering whether to approve these facilities. Mayo stressed he wanted to present "an honest, sourced picture" without promoting or alarming the public, noting that accurate information helps communities make informed choices about whether to welcome data centers to their regions.

Mayo's research found that data centers may actually lower electricity rates overall by spreading grid costs across more consumers. He also found that modern cooling systems use minimal water and that noise concerns are manageable through proper setbacks from residential areas. Multiple data center projects are underway in North Dakota, including Applied Digital's nearly completed 3 billion dollar facility near Harwood. Policymakers should evaluate community engagement, power sources, cooling systems and distance from homes before approving projects, Mayo recommended.
